R0040.title: Carding Attack
R0040.definition: Verifying the validity of stolen payment card credentials through bulk login authentication.
R0040.description: Using a merchant's complete login credential verification process to validate stolen payment cards or accounts. Since the value of stolen accounts is unknown, carding attacks can be used to assess payment card value. The source of credential data may be third-party application breaches, third-party payment channel leaks, or purchases from black markets.
R0040.influence: Payment card or account credential information is stolen.

observables: The login endpoint shows a surge of batch attempts from many different accounts originating from the same IP range within a short window, with a spike in failure rate
A single device fingerprint attempts to log into a large number of different accounts within a short window
Account and card number combinations in login requests exhibit leaked-database characteristics, such as concentrated BIN ranges or expiry date enumeration
After successful login, the session immediately jumps to value-assessment endpoints such as payment, card binding, or balance inquiry
Multiple accounts initiate small-amount test payments or query available credit shortly after logging in
